features.text: The patient has had pain on the right side of the belly under the ribs for several weeks.
The pain is described as squeezing and severe, located under the ribs on the right side.
The pain comes and goes, and is associated with nausea.
The pain occurs after eating, either immediately or a couple of hours later.
The patient has not experienced jaundice, dark urine, or pale stools.
The patient has not had recent weight loss or changes in bowel habits.
The patient has not experienced fever, chills, or changes in bowel habits such as diarrhea or constipation.
The pain does not radiate to the back or shoulder.
The patient has a family history of gallbladder disease, with both parents having had gallbladder issues and surgeries.
The patient had an ultrasound that found gallstones in the gallbladder.
The patient was advised to avoid high-fat foods, but this has not significantly reduced the pain.
The patient has not had any recent episodes of severe pain requiring medical attention or medication.
The patient has not experienced changes in bowel habits since the onset of the abdominal pain.

The patient is not aware of having undergone any blood tests, such as a complete blood count (CBC), liver function tests (LFTs), or inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP, amylase, lipase), since the gallstone diagnosis.
